content:
In its current form, the pursuit feels both too niche and too limited, as not only is it tied to the dimensional image, which is exceptionally rare without the Chaos ring, but it also only comes out after the exalt, which, in majority of cases, is already a killing blow.

While I understand that adding the pursuit to the base kit could offset the game balance, it does feel rather lame for such a gorgeous animation to only be accessible under very rare circumstances, so I would still like to make the following suggestion:
Instead of having the pursuit go off after the exalt, have it deal significantly less damage, but trigger at the start of every turn, as long as you have the Great Blade: Whalefall in hand.
I do believe that this trigger condition would make GLotan's gameplay feel a lot more interactive and open more potential strategies, as right now, once you achieve the condition for creating Great Blade: Whalefall, there isn't much for the team to do outside of simply waiting while stacking the bonus damage from Deadly Duel.

But ultimately, please don't lock such a cool animation behind a rare relic, even if it means making the pursuit barely deal any damage 
Thank you to whoever ends up reading this!! <:meow:1506486299098480690>

Naturally it would need to do less damage, however the dimensional image could still stay the same, triggering the big hit of the pursuit after exalt. This would just allow the pursuit to be triggered naturally allowing full usage of GLotan's kit, without locking an entire aspect of the character behind an RNG mechanic, as without D-tide rings, you cannot gurantee you will find her dimensional image. As far as I'm aware no other image in the game locks such a mechanic behind it, with most being extra passives or stat changes.

While the numbers need to be tuned if it is to be triggered more, I believe a balance could be found, allowing the character's full design to be utilized, as well as rewarding the risk/reward playstyle she already supports due to scaling on enemy damage. <:Casiah_wink:1356053053568192717>

thread_title: Divine Realms, Aliemus Costs and other Future Worries

content:
To be honest, I think that while Divine realms are interesting and do provide much more to the teambuilding scene, the fact that many if not all of the older awakeners are based around the old realms, and sometimes running a team without divine realms/newer realms is just more enjoyable. I'm not against divine realms, but rather the idea that all future units will always only be wielding divine realms. Like bagels said above, if there are only these options going forward, what happens to the older characters? Many of the base realm/older characters are deeply beloved, and if this does progress forward, does it mean that they'll have to be left behind?

Same with higher base aliemus; it was an interesting addition at first, but when every single newer unit now has it, the game starts feeling clunkier to play, and older systems stop functioning to the same extent. I haven't explored the Absolute Axioms as well, but if they truly are a primary source of Aliemus for those awakeners with high base aliemus, then does it mean that we're expected to go all the way for them? That would restrict accessibility and general enjoyability of the game for anyone who isn't spending larger amounts for these characters they enjoy. 

A more personal query I have though, is with the Ultra Realm. Starting with the release of Clementine, we have had no units with the Leap mechanic, and after two units (Clem & Castor), the Quasar mechanic disappeared as well. In my experience, the Leap and Quasar mechanics have felt like a core part of the Ultra Realm, as part of the first-card-per-turn system. The disappearance of these mechanics have lead to the newer Ultra units (Pollux and Arachne) to feel less familiar and interesting. Are there any plans in the future to bring back either of these mechanics, or can we assume that they're gone for good? If so, then what happens to the units that already have them?
